record.paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
record.original_question: For quartic threefolds, is there a categorical Torelli theorem that reconstructs the threefold, up to isomorphism or an appropriate Torelli equivalence, from its Kuznetsov component and the relevant categorical structures?

evidence.quote: Is there a version of the Categorical Torelli theorem

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^4_{\mathbb{C}}$ be a smooth quartic hypersurface (a Fano threefold of Picard rank one, index one, and genus three). The bounded derived category $D^b(X)$ of coherent sheaves on $X$ admits a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(X),\ \mathcal{O}_X,\ \mathcal{O}_X(1) \rangle,$$
where the Kuznetsov component $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is defined as the right orthogonal $\langle \mathcal{O}_X,\mathcal{O}_X(1)\rangle^\perp$. The component $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-linear triangulated category, equipped with its natural enhancement, Serre functor, and additional categorical structures (such as a distinguished Bridgeland stability condition when one is fixed).

Prove or disprove the following Categorical Torelli statement: if $X$ and $X'$ are two smooth quartic threefolds in $\mathbb{P}^4$ such that there is a $\mathbb{C}$-linear equivalence (of Fourier–Mukai type) $\mathcal{K}u(X) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(X')$ compatible with the relevant categorical structures, then $X \cong X'$ as projective varieties. Equivalently, formulate and establish a version of the Categorical Torelli theorem reconstructing a smooth quartic threefold up to isomorphism (or up to an appropriate Torelli-type equivalence) from its Kuznetsov component.
artifact.category_tag: Categorical Torelli theorems for Fano threefolds
artifact.status_search_result: Partial categorical Torelli statements are known for smooth Fano hypersurfaces (including quartic threefolds) under the assumption that the equivalence between Kuznetsov components is of Fourier–Mukai type, and refined categorical Torelli results have been obtained for other index-one prime Fano threefolds via Brill–Noether techniques. However, no unconditional Categorical Torelli theorem for the smooth quartic threefold (index 1, genus 3 Fano hypersurface in $\mathbb{P}^4$) appears in the literature; it is still listed as an open question.

status_evidence.title: IVHS via Kuznetsov components and categorical Torelli theorems for weighted hypersurfaces
status_evidence.snippet: For smooth hypersurfaces of degree d ≤ n in P^n ... if Ku(X) ≃ Ku(X') with equivalence given by a Fourier–Mukai functor, then X ≅ X'.
status_evidence.claim: A conditional (Fourier–Mukai type) categorical Torelli result covers quartic threefolds, but the unconditional statement remains open.

status_evidence.title: Brill–Noether theory for Kuznetsov components and refined categorical Torelli
status_evidence.snippet: Every index one prime Fano threefold of genus g ≥ 6 can be reconstructed as a Brill–Noether locus inside a Bridgeland moduli space of stable objects in its Kuznetsov component.
status_evidence.claim: Refined categorical Torelli theorems are known for index-one prime Fano threefolds of genus at least 6, leaving lower-genus cases (such as genus 3 quartic threefolds) less complete.

status_evidence.title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Is there a version of the Categorical Torelli theorem [for quartic threefolds]
status_evidence.claim: The question of a categorical Torelli theorem for quartic threefolds is explicitly posed as an open problem.
